verifiedFacts: Houston average summer relative humidity exceeds 75%, generating 5 to 20 gallons of condensate daily from a standard 3- to 5-ton residential HVAC system.

findings.targetAudience: Houston prospective home buyers and real estate investors in 1960-1990 homes
findings.seasonalRelevance: Year-round; peaks during spring and summer homebuying surge

verifiedFacts: A hydrostatic test requires inflating an inflatable test ball at the home's main sewer cleanout and filling the building drain system with water up to slab level to detect slab leaks.
Under Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC) guidelines, home inspectors cannot perform hydrostatic testing; only a licensed Master Plumber (RMP) can authorize and execute a hydrostatic pressure test.
estimates: A standalone hydrostatic drain test in Houston typically ranges between $350 and $700 depending on cleanout accessibility.

findings.topic: Preventing Winter Pipe Bursts & Outdoor Spigot Freezes in Houston
relatedKeywords: how to protect pipes freezing houston

findings.targetAudience: Homeowners in Greater Houston preparing for sudden polar vortex freezes
findings.seasonalRelevance: Critical in November, December, January, February

verifiedFacts: Houston homes built on slab foundations often have CPVC or copper supply lines running through uninsulated exterior brick veneers or vented attics where temperatures drop below 28°F during arctic fronts.
Water expands by approximately 9% upon freezing, generating upwards of 2,000 psi internal pressure that fractures rigid pipes.
estimates: Burst pipe emergency repairs in attic spaces often require coordinated sheetrock and insulation remediation.
